openDecisions.question: Switch the positive-day levels from peak-based to quantile-based?
openDecisions.specSays: Section 13, line 317: allowed ('дозволено перейти') only if the current peak-based quantization makes almost all positive cells equally light because of an outlier. It stays presentation-only.
openDecisions.codebaseSays: toLevel at apps/web/src/features/delivery/model/statistics-calendar.ts:193-196 is Math.ceil(value / peak * 4). A user with one 40-order day and many 1-2 order days gets level 1 for every ordinary day, so the flattening is real for realistic data, not hypothetical. Changing it touches the existing level tests at statistics-calendar.test.ts:186-210.
openDecisions.recommendation: Yes, do T28. Keep peak for the top level (busiest day stays level 4) and use the positive-day distribution for levels 1-3. Cost is one pure function plus its tests; benefit is that the block stops reading as empty for the most common purchase pattern.
openDecisions.answer: ACCEPTED (user, 2026-09-10): switch positive-day levels to quantile-based. Peak day stays level 4; levels 1-3 come from the distribution of positive days. Presentation only - backend untouched, tooltip always shows exact counts. T28 becomes mandatory.

openDecisions.question: Add the optional right-edge fade on the mobile scroll viewport?
openDecisions.specSays: Section 16, line 386: 'Опційно можна додати subtle edge fade справа'.
openDecisions.codebaseSays: No existing edge-fade pattern in the statistics slice; the reading heatmap does not have one either. It would be a new one-off visual primitive.
openDecisions.recommendation: Skip it for this pass. Scroll affordance is already given by the cut-off week column, and a new one-off gradient is the kind of thing CLAUDE.md §8.15 calls preemptive. Revisit if a real mobile check shows users missing the scroll.
openDecisions.answer: DECLINED (user, 2026-09-10): skip the right-edge fade. The clipped week column is affordance enough. T29 stays out of scope.

openDecisions.question: Which population does calendarCoverage count, and where does it hang on the response?
openDecisions.specSays: Section 8, lines 174-182: prefers { ordersInScope, ordersWithOrderDate, ordersWithoutOrderDate }, and allows an equivalent structure that fits the current contracts. Section 15 line 371: coverage is understood within the actually loaded source.
openDecisions.codebaseSays: buildOrderDaily is called with includedOrders (apps/api/src/modules/delivery/domain/order-statistics.ts:125), i.e. after the includeCancelled/currency/store filters. meta already groups completeness info (activeSource/currentSource, packages/shared/src/orders.ts BookOrderStatisticsMetaSchema), but meta is about source truncation, while coverage is about the calendar's own population. computeBookOrderStatistics returns Omit<BookOrderStatisticsView,'meta'> (order-statistics.ts:59), so a top-level key lands naturally in the domain where daily is built; putting it in meta would mean plumbing it through delivery-statistics.service.ts instead.
openDecisions.recommendation: Count includedOrders (the exact array daily is built from) and put calendarCoverage at the top level of BookOrderStatisticsViewSchema, next to daily, with the spec's three field names. This keeps the note's number honest: it describes precisely the orders the calendar could have drawn.
openDecisions.answer: ACCEPTED (user, 2026-09-10): calendarCoverage sits top-level next to daily, computed in the delivery domain over includedOrders (post-filter), with the spec field names ordersInScope / ordersWithOrderDate / ordersWithoutOrderDate.

openDecisions.question: Where does the 'Бюджет на книги' card go in the new order?
openDecisions.specSays: Section 1 lists KPI, then dynamics + pulse, then the calendar, then specialised analytics. The budget card is not mentioned at all.
openDecisions.codebaseSays: It currently sits between KPI and the dynamics row (apps/web/src/features/delivery/components/delivery-statistics.tsx:276) and is asserted in SECTION_ORDER at delivery-statistics.test.tsx:31.
openDecisions.recommendation: Leave it where it is. It is KPI-adjacent, not specialised analytics, and moving it is scope the spec never asked for. The spec's real constraint - calendar immediately after dynamics + pulse - is satisfied either way.
openDecisions.answer: ACCEPTED (user, 2026-09-10): the "������ �� �����" card keeps its current position between KPI and dynamics. SECTION_ORDER keeps it there.

openDecisions.question: Ship a mobile-specific 13px cell, or one 14px size everywhere?
openDecisions.specSays: Section 4, lines 77-80: mobile is 14x14 by default, 13x13 is tolerated only 'за крайньої потреби', and never back to 11x11.
openDecisions.codebaseSays: The card body is already inside a page container with padding; at 360px a full-year canvas is ~53 weeks * 17px = ~900px, so it scrolls regardless of whether the cell is 13 or 14. Dropping to 13 buys nothing once horizontal scroll exists.
openDecisions.recommendation: One 14px size at every breakpoint. A responsive size would add a second source of truth for the pitch that the month-label offsets also depend on.
openDecisions.answer: ACCEPTED (user, 2026-09-10): one 14px cell size at every breakpoint. No responsive pitch - a single pitch stays the only source of truth for month-label offsets.

openDecisions.question: A non-zero day with zero drill-down destinations: keep the focusable tooltip button, or make it a static cell?
openDecisions.specSays: Section 7, lines 140-141: '0 destinations - Cell informational/static'. Section 17, line 409: keyboard focus only on interactive non-zero cells; line 412: the tooltip must be reachable on focus.
openDecisions.codebaseSays: statistics-calendar.tsx:230-237 currently renders a focusable <button type="button"> with no action, purely to host the tooltip. This is also the state every non-zero day falls into while the source is truncated (line 213 zeroes the links), and the existing test at line 154 asserts that button exists.
openDecisions.recommendation: Keep it focusable, but make it explicitly non-actionable: keep the button element so the tooltip and its counts stay keyboard-reachable, and give it aria-disabled plus no menu/link. A truly static span would hide the day's counts from keyboard users, which contradicts section 17 line 412 more sharply than it satisfies section 7's 'static'. Whichever way this goes, T21 and T26 must state it.
openDecisions.answer: ACCEPTED (user, 2026-09-10): a non-zero day with zero destinations stays focusable but explicitly non-actionable (button + aria-disabled, no menu, no link), so keyboard users still reach the counts in the truncated state. Encode in T21 and T26.

openDecisions.question: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size requires 24x24px targets or 24px between centres; spec section 4 mandates 14x14 cells at a 17px pitch. Measured live: size 14x14, closest pair 17px apart.
openDecisions.answer: ACCEPTED (user, 2026-09-10): keep the 14px cells the spec asks for and claim the SC 2.5.8 "Equivalent" exception - the same day drill-down is reachable through the in-transit page own date filters (orderedFrom/orderedTo). Recorded as a deliberate documented decision, not an oversight.
